svg.title: Inside a session of Open QA Stack
svg.desc: A session in detail. It reads and checks its configuration, checks that the sources, the applications and the model answer, then maps the knowledge: a survey finds the sources that changed, a source cartographer, a document cartographer and an application explorer read each of them, a domain writer groups their elements by business domain, and an orchestrator puts them together into a knowledge base. The design goes by rounds, level by level — smoke, functional, business, cross-application, end-to-end, then visual — until 40 tests or 3 rounds that bring nothing new. A planner explores the application and proposes a plan, which the harness checks rule by rule and refuses with a reason; a plan reviewer sets aside what is already tested. For each scenario, a writer writes the test and its page objects and runs it three times; the harness checks how it closes; a coherence reviewer and a code reviewer check it; it is committed on a branch. The whole suite then runs, with a verdict per test. The test repository, the instance and the traces keep everything. People review each test — validate, set aside, restore, or ask a correction the writer makes — handle defects from open to fixed to closed, run campaigns from planned to closed, and keep a memory of instructions, corrections and notes the agents read before every task.
